# v1.1.0-dev.72 — Monitors the right shape, in a window that stays put

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.71`.

Three fixes to the Display editor. One of them was a real
distortion rather than a matter of taste.

## Your Monitors Were The Wrong Shape

The picker draws your monitors to scale. It wasn't.

The drawing was told to fill the width available and separately
told not to exceed a certain height. When both applied, the height
won and everything got squashed flat. Measured on a two-monitor
desk: **2.6 times too wide**, so a normal 16:9 screen was drawn at
nearly 5:1.

That's why landscape looked stretched and portrait looked wrong.

The width is now limited by the height too. The picture can never be
squeezed out of shape. A 16:9 monitor measures 1.783 against a true
1.778, and a portrait one 0.564 against 0.563. The remaining
fraction of a percent is the hairline that keeps two touching
monitors from reading as a single box.

## Space Around Them

The monitors sat flush against the edge of their container. There's
a margin on every side now.

## The Window Stops Jumping

Changing a resolution, opening **By hand**, typing a size into it,
going back to the list, picking the other monitor: every one of
those used to nudge the window taller or shorter. All of them now
measure exactly the same height.

Two things hold it still. The by-hand boxes keep their space when
they're closed rather than collapsing. The summary at the top reserves
room for everything it can ever show, instead of growing a line the
moment you configure a display.

The compact picker in Settings still collapses, because a table
cell shouldn't carry a permanent gap.

One exception, on purpose: the Keep or Revert bar still makes the
window taller when it appears. That happens after you press **Apply
now** rather than from choosing an option. Holding that space open
permanently would cost more than the jump does.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
